posts.what: How many pieces you published in the period. Volume is the input you control most.
posts.good: Your weekly target, every week. A streak matters more than a big week.

impressions.what: How many times your posts were shown, added up. Each platform calls it reach, views or impressions; use the biggest honest number it gives you and use the same one every time.
impressions.good: Growing week on week. The number itself matters less than the direction.

engagementRate.what: Likes, comments, shares and saves, divided by reach. Says whether the people who saw it cared.
engagementRate.good: Above 2% is fine, above 5% is good. Saves and shares are worth more than likes.

follows.what: New followers your posts brought, added up from what you typed on each post.
follows.good: Any. Compare it to reach: a post that brings followers at a high rate is worth repeating.

leads.what: People who moved to Lead in the period: they asked about working with you, or gave you a way to reach them.
leads.good: Your weekly target. If reach is up and leads are flat, the ask on the posts is the thing to change.

outreach.what: Messages you sent to people, by lane: warm, cold, from content, paid, referral. This is the work nobody sees.
outreach.good: The weekly target, done daily. Twenty-five a week is five a working day.

conversations.what: People who replied, or who reached out first, in the period. Counted once a person.
conversations.good: A third of the people you reach out to. Below one in six, change the message, not the volume.

replyRate.what: People who replied divided by people you reached out to.

calls.what: Calls booked in the period, from a stage change to Call booked or a touch marked booked.

clients.what: People who became clients in the period.
clients.good: Any. Note where each one came from; that lane gets more of your time.

revenue.what: The value you typed for each person who became a client in the period.
revenue.good: Only what was actually agreed. No forecasts here.

hours.what: Minutes you typed on each post, added up. The cost side.
hours.good: Falling per lead over time. If it rises for three months, the format is wrong.

hoursPerLead.what: Content hours divided by leads. What a lead costs you in time.
hoursPerLead.good: Falling. There is no right number; only your last one.

streak.what: Weeks in a row you hit the posting target, counting back from this week.

funnel.what: Each step of the way from a stranger to a client, as a count and as a share of the step before.
funnel.good: Find the step with the worst drop. That is the only thing to work on this month.

due.what: People whose next touch is today or overdue, from their stage's rhythm or the date you set.
due.good: Empty by the end of the day.

date.means: The day it was published, not the day you made it.

channel.means: One platform a row. The same video on two platforms is two rows.

format.means: So you can see which formats earn their time.

pillar.means: A short topic word: money, family, behind the scenes, a story. Use the same words every time so they group.

hook.means: The words on screen or the opening sentence. The thing people decide on.

cta.plain: What did you ask people to do?
cta.means: Leads come from asks. No ask, no lead, and that is fine sometimes.

minutes.plain: How long did it take to make?
minutes.means: Rough minutes. Leave it blank if you do not know; a blank is not a zero.

impressions.means: Views, reach or impressions from the platform's own numbers. Pick one and stick to it.

results.means: Come back a few days later and type the platform's numbers. Blank means not checked yet.

name.means: The name you would use to them.

stage.means: Stranger, follower, in conversation, lead, call booked, client, advocate, or not now.

cadence.means: Days between touches. Blank uses the stage's usual rhythm. Zero means never.

nextAt.means: A date you set overrides the rhythm. Clear it to go back to the rhythm.

value.means: Only for a client. The agreed amount in dollars.

lane.means: Warm (they know you), cold (they do not), from content (a post brought them), paid, referral.

outcome.means: No reply yet, they replied, a call got booked, they bought, or not now.

words: How many times a post was shown.
Likes, comments, shares and saves, together.
One message, comment, call or meeting with one person.
Where the person came from: warm, cold, content, paid, referral.
A person who replied or reached out first.
Someone who asked about working with you or gave you a way to reach them.
The steps from stranger to client, each as a share of the one before.
How many days between touches for a person.
Weeks in a row the posting target was hit.
Where this week's number should be by now if the week ends on target.
